To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
customers who have experienced bad customer service do not differ from customers who experienced good customer service with regard to the factors that they take into account in their evaluation.

“Customers that experience bad customer services do take into account all the variables in their evaluation of their relationship with a service provider, however the weights they place on each factor and the strength of the relationship between variables are different than the ones of customers that experience good service”.Originality/value – This study is the first to compare the impact of bad and good customer services on the variables that are known in the literature to drive revenue, such as customer satisfaction, perceived service quality and customer commitment.

the perception of customer service does not affect customer satisfaction, perceived service value, or commitment, but it does affect perceived relative attractiveness.Originality/value – The study is one of the first to examine the impact of varying degrees of service on customer satisfaction and commitment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of customers' perception on customer service on commitment, customer satisfaction, and perceived relative attractiveness and the results indicate that customer service has an impact on all of the variables.

the question as to whether the perception of customer service has a different impact on customers' satisfaction, commitment, and perceived relative attractiveness, depending on the degree of customer service (good/bad).

the question of the impact of customer service on performance and the answer is that it does matter but it matters more to customers that have experienced bad customer service than to customers that have had good service.Research limitations/implications – This study is based on a single industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the impact of customer service is different for customers that experience bad customer services compared to customers who experience good customer services.Research limitations/implications – The sample was limited in size and to bank customers only.
the customer service experience has an important effect on customer satisfaction, which in turn affects perceived relative attractiveness, which in turn has a positive effect on customer commitment.

the impact of the customer service variables on commitment and perceived attractiveness is different for customers that experience bad customer or good customer service.Originality/value – The paper provides new insight into the impact of varying degrees of service on customers' perception of service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
customer service is important for customer satisfaction and customer commitment.
customer service is an important driver of performance and that the impact of the service is dependent on how the service is perceived by the customers.
the customer's perception of the level of customer service provided by the bank has a strong effect on the customer's perception about the bank and the bank's performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of customers’ perception of customer service varies with the level of customer service experienced.
customer service is a complex phenomenon.
the effect of customer service is not as strong as expected and that the effect of the perceived service quality and perceived value on customer commitment is stronger.
